# Flowie

> Flowie is a fast, keyboard-first outliner for macOS (13 Ventura or later, Apple silicon and Intel). Every bullet is a page you can zoom into; it has `[[` links with backlinks, mirrors, tags, a daily journal, native LaTeX math, instant search, and a built-in MCP server for AI assistants. All data stays in one local SQLite database on the Mac: no account, no cloud, no tracking. It is free software under the GPL-3.0-or-later, written in Rust on GPUI, with English and Simplified Chinese (简体中文) interfaces.

Key facts:

- Platform: macOS only (no Windows, Linux, iOS or web version). No sync between devices; the outline is a local file.
- Get it: the [Mac App Store]({{ site.app_store_url }}) (signed, sandboxed, auto-updating), the open-source version from [GitHub Releases]({{ site.github_url }}/releases/latest) (`Flowie-<version>-macos.zip`, not notarized), or Homebrew: `brew install --cask wesleyel/tap/flowie`.
- Migrating: imports OPML, Markdown and plain text, including Workflowy exports; exports Markdown, OPML and plain text.
- Math: inline `$…$` and display `$$…$$` LaTeX (KaTeX-compatible), rendered natively while typing.
- AI: an MCP server (`Flowie mcp`, stdio) with tools search, read, starred, create, update, complete, move, delete, journal and open. Access is Off / Read only / Read & write in Settings → Agent; every AI edit is live and undoable. Register with Claude Code: `claude mcp add flowie -- /Applications/Flowie.app/Contents/MacOS/Flowie mcp`.
- Keyboard: every action has a shortcut and every shortcut can be remapped, including mouse side buttons; ⌘P quick open; `/` command menu.
- Good fit for: people who think in nested lists, Workflowy users who want a local, offline Mac app, students and researchers who write math in notes, and anyone who wants an AI assistant to read and edit their outline.
